text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Suleyman Demirel criticises conservative Tansu Ciller for her outburst against him over the government search.
- Opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz extends an olive branch to Ciller, offering to forget the past conflicts and reach an agreement over forming a new government.
- Ciller will suggest Yilmaz join a coalition with her True Path Party and the Welfare Party of Prime Minister of Necmettin Erbakan.
- Erbakan in state of shock at nomination of Yilmaz as prime minister-designate. The Islamist leader may now not be able to prevent the banning of his party by the constitutional court.
- Yilmaz tries to woo conservatives from rival party.
- The political uncertainty is damaging Turkey's prized relations with the European Union.
- The military wants changes in the state-run Religious Affairs Directorate.
- A leading businessman says there is no democracy in Turkey, but a selfish and authoritarian system run by an elite in Ankara.
